# The Hunter's Bow Drawn Across the Sky

## Scripture
**"He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the human heart; yet no one can fathom what God has done from beginning to end." — Ecclesiastes 3:11**

## Reflection
On crisp October evenings, look toward the eastern horizon and you'll find Orion rising—the Hunter, with his famous three-star belt and the glowing nebula that hangs from his sword. Ancient stargazers saw a mighty warrior in these stars. But one detail is easy to miss: the faint curve of stars that form his bow, drawn back as if ready to release an arrow that never flies.

Day after day, night after night, the Hunter draws his bow but the arrow never leaves the string. It has been this way for thousands of years—unchanging, patient, suspended in the sky.

Solomon reminds us that God "has made everything beautiful in its time." So much of our lives feels like that bow: drawn taut, waiting, poised for something that hasn't yet arrived. We strain toward the release, wondering when the arrow will finally fly. But God's timing isn't ours. The waiting itself is part of His beautiful work.

He has set eternity in our hearts—a longing for something beyond this moment. That ache isn't a flaw; it's a compass pointing home.

## Prayer
Lord, when I feel like a bowstring stretched and waiting, remind me that You make all things beautiful in Your time. Teach me to trust Your patient hand. Amen.
